prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Columbus after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Columbus Ohio for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but before I give firm names I need one quick thing: do you want a large firm with lots of resources or a smaller local firm that will give you more one‑on‑one attention? Also (briefly) were you seriously injured, is fault disputed, and where in Columbus did the crash happen? That will let me tailor recommendations.

If you want immediate next steps, here’s a practical plan you can use right now plus how to pick specific firms to call.

Who to call (how to find specific firms)
- Use the Columbus Bar Association Lawyer Referral Service and the Ohio State Bar Association directory to get vetted referrals (they’ll match you to personal injury attorneys experienced with car wrecks).
- Search for personal injury attorneys in Columbus with strong trial experience and contingency-fee arrangements. Look for:
  - AV‑Rated or similarly peer‑reviewed credentials (Martindale‑Hubbell).
  - Client reviews on Google/Avvo/Better Business Bureau.
  - A proven record handling car-accident claims (not just general practice).
- Call at least 3 firms to compare. If you want, tell me whether you prefer boutique/local or a national firm and I’ll suggest names I know have offices or reputations to check.

What to ask when you call (so you can compare quickly)
- Do you handle car-accident/personal injury cases full time?
- How long have you handled auto-injury claims in Columbus/Franklin County?
- Do you handle cases on contingency (no fee unless you recover)? What is your contingency percentage and what costs would be deducted?
- Do you go to trial, or do you settle most cases? How many trials did you personally try in the last 3 years?
- Who will be my main point of contact (attorney or paralegal)? How often will I get updates?
- Have you handled cases with my injury type (e.g., whiplash, broken bones, traumatic brain injury)?
- Estimated timeline and what outcome range they think is realistic (they’ll give a range, not a promise).
- Ask for references or case results (they can’t guarantee a result but can share representative settlements/verdicts).

What to bring to the free consultation
- Police report or crash report number.
- Photos of the scene/vehicles/visible injuries.
- Medical records and bills, or at least the provider names and dates of treatment.
- Insurance information for all parties.
- Any correspondence from insurance companies (including recorded statements).
- Names and contact info of witnesses.

Red flags to avoid
- Any firm that pressures you to sign immediately without allowing you to review the agreement.
- Guarantees of a specific settlement amount.
- Poor or no transparency about fee structure or who will handle your case.

If you want, I can:
- Suggest 4–6 specific Columbus firms (national and local) to call based on whether you prefer big-firm resources or a local boutique — tell me which you prefer and give the neighborhood/ZIP or injury severity.
- Draft a short script you can read when you call so you get consistent info from each firm.

Which would you prefer — specific firm names now (and do you prefer national or local/boutique), or help contacting the Columbus Bar referral and vetting firms?
